---
title: "2. Data overview"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
box::use(show = projlib/show, util = projlib/msdial_utils)
raw <- tut$raw
tr <- tut$to_report
cd <- SumExp::col_df(raw)
rd <- SumExp::row_df(raw)
```

**Data overview** is available as the file is read and gives an overview of what is in the data.
Can be used to double check that the data was formatted by the app according to your wishes.

## 2.1 Samples by category
Every sample by its category (from the `File type` row) and class. The calibration samples are
counted together here; their levels are in 2.2.

```{r}
#| label: table-2-1
catg <- util$ctrl_smpl_cat(raw)
catg[catg == ""] <- "Sample"
d <- tibble::tibble(Category = catg, Class = ifelse(catg == "CalCurve", "All levels", cd$Class)) |>
  dplyr::count(Category, Class, name = "Number of samples") |>
  dplyr::mutate(Percent = paste0(round(100 * `Number of samples` / sum(`Number of samples`), 1), "%"))
tut_table(d)
```


::: {.callout-tip}
- **Check the categories**: blanks, calibration samples (`CalCurve`), QCs and study samples
  (`Sample`). A QC counted as a study sample, or a blank missing, means a wrong `File type` in the
  file.
- **QC classes** are the QC materials; at least two replicates of a class are needed for the RSD%
  in 3.8 and for choosing the best normalization.
:::

## 2.2 Calibration levels
The number of calibration samples per concentration level (read from the names, e.g. `Cal0-5` =
0.5), per batch and in total.

```{r}
#| label: table-2-2
tut_table(show$calib_samples_per_batch(raw))
```


::: {.callout-tip}
- **Double-check replicates if they exist** in every batch. The LOD/LLOQ method *mean + SD* needs at
  least two zero calibrants (`Cal0`), and the RSD% option at least two replicates of each level; a
  batch without them uses the curve of all batches together.
- **A level missing in one batch** shortens that batch's curve.
:::

## 2.3 Classes of analytes
The features by their `Comment`: targeted compounds (`Quant`), internal standards (`IS`), the
volumetric internal standard (`vIS`) and non-targeted features. (The app lists `Quant\…` and
`IS\…` with their class names; they are counted together here.)

```{r}
#| label: table-2-3
v <- util$std_type(raw)
v <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(v) | v == "" ~ "Not targeted", util$is_targeted_feature(v) ~ "Quant",
                      util$is_internal_std(v) ~ "IS", TRUE ~ v)
tut_table(tibble::tibble(`Standard type` = v) |> dplyr::count(`Standard type`, name = "Number of features") |>
            dplyr::mutate(Percent = paste0(round(100 * `Number of features` / sum(`Number of features`), 1), "%")))
```


## 2.4 Features by m/z and retention time
Every feature at its retention time and m/z. After processing, the targeted compounds are coloured
by their **outcome**: *Quantified* (green), *Valid curve, not found in samples* (orange), *No valid
calibration* (red), or *Removed* by the blank filter or the QC RSD% filter (crosses). The internal
standards are black diamonds, the volumetric IS a blue one; the non-targeted features (grey) can be
switched on in the legend.

```{r}
#| label: figure-2-4
blk <- util$mat_id_of_blank_subtracted(tr[["best normalization"]])
calib_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(Filter(\(x) !is.null(x$concn), tut$proc[[blk]]), function(x) {
  tibble::as_tibble(SumExp::row_df(x$concn), rownames = "feature_id") |> dplyr::select(feature_id, to_export, has_proper_range)
}))
rem <- tr[["removed features"]]
removed <- rem[rem$mat_id == tr[["best normalization"]] & rem$targeted, ]
show$plotly_mz_rt_map(show$mz_rt_outcome(rd, calib_rows, removed), height = 520)
```


::: {.callout-tip}
- **Clusters of compounds that were not quantified** in one region (e.g. early retention times) point to a
  chromatographic or matrix problem there.
- **Internal standards** should cover the retention-time range of the targeted compounds: the
  *Closest RT* normalization uses the nearest one.
:::

## 2.5 Distribution of m/z
The number of features per m/z, in bins of 0.5. Hover over a bar for its range; drag to zoom.

```{r}
#| label: figure-2-5
show$plotly_binned_hist(rd$mz, binwidth = 0.5, x_title = "m/z")
```



## 2.6 Distribution of intensities
All raw peak areas of all features and samples: in linear scale (left) and in log scale (right,
positive values only). The note tells how many values are zero or missing.

```{r}
#| label: figure-2-6
show$plotly_value_distribution(SumExp::metadata(raw)$value_bins %||% raw[["raw"]])
```



::: {.callout-tip}
- **The log panel** shows the dynamic range of the data; most peak areas usually span several
  orders of magnitude.
- **Many zeros** are normal for non-targeted features (not found in every sample), but a large
  share of zeros in the internal standards fails them (see 3.2).
:::
